title: Thirteen years
hook: exile, disguise, the year in hiding

segments.voice: Yesterday: Draupadi's sari, the cloth that wouldn't end and the question nobody answered. Your line was unending. Did you notice anyone being shamed? Day seventy-four.

You'd think, after all that, the Pandavas would never touch dice again. They're freed by Draupadi's wishes, and they head home. And they're called back. One more game. One throw. The loser goes into the forest for twelve years, and then must spend a thirteenth year in hiding, somewhere in the world, undiscovered. If anyone recognizes them in that year, they start all over again. Yudhishthira plays. Yudhishthira loses. And five royal brothers, and a queen, walk into the forest with nothing.
screen: `CALLED BACK FOR ONE MORE THROW.` → `TWELVE YEARS IN THE FOREST.` → `ONE MORE YEAR, UNSEEN.`

segments.voice: The twelve forest years fill a huge part of the Mahabharata: sages, pilgrimages, stories inside stories. Near the end of them, the brothers, desperately thirsty, find a lake guarded by a spirit, a yaksha, who says: answer my questions before you drink. Four brothers drink anyway and fall dead. Yudhishthira stops and answers. The most famous question: what is the greatest wonder in the world? And his answer, roughly: that every day people die all around us, and the rest of us live as if we never will. He answers well enough that his brothers are given back their lives. Then the thirteenth year. They go to the court of a king called Virata and hide in plain sight, each one disguised as the last thing you'd expect. Yudhishthira, the man who lost everything at dice, becomes the king's dice companion. Bhima, the strongest man alive, becomes a cook. Arjuna, the great archer, lives as a dance teacher named Brihannala, in women's clothes, because of an old curse that now turns out to be a gift. The twins look after horses and cattle. And Draupadi, the queen, becomes a maid to the queen. It isn't safe. A powerful general of the court harasses Draupadi, and Bhima kills him in secret. But the year runs out, and they're not caught. Look at the disguises again: each of them hides inside a smaller version of their own life. Sometimes the only way through is to disappear for a while: to become smaller, quieter, someone else, and wait. The year of hiding isn't the end of who they are. It's a year of carrying who they are, secretly.
screen: `THE YAKSHA'S QUESTIONS AT THE LAKE.` · `THE GREATEST WONDER.` · `HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT.` · `A YEAR OF CARRYING WHO THEY ARE.`

segments.voice: Sit, and let your breathing slow. Think of a season when you had to hide. Maybe you hid what you believed, or who you loved, or how bad things were. Maybe you had to take a job far beneath what you could do, or keep quiet to stay safe. Remember what you carried in secret the whole time. Don't judge that season. It got you through. Then think: is someone around you hiding right now? What might they be carrying that nobody sees? The bell holds the time.
Thirteen years. Twelve in the forest, and one in hiding, in plain sight, at a king's court.
Your line: the year of hiding. Today, be gentle with someone who seems smaller or quieter than they are. You don't know what they're carrying. Day seventy-four.

howItsDone: The Yaksha's questions to Yudhishthira are often retold and taught as a dialogue on dharma, and the Virata Parva, the book of the year in hiding, is traditionally recited in some regions to pray for rain.

fork.setup: you're Yudhishthira, dying of thirst at a lake. a spirit says: answer my questions before you drink. your brothers didn't, and they're lying dead. what do you do?
fork.reveal: he stops and answers every question, and the yaksha gives his brothers back their lives.

original.note: Sanskrit: ajnata (unknown) + vasa (dwelling). Living unrecognized: the year in hiding.

trapdoor: what you thought: a long punishment.
what it means: twelve years in the forest and a year of hiding in plain sight, carrying who they are in secret.
what a scholar hears: ajnatavasa, living unknown. the Virata Parva, the book of that year, is recited in some regions to pray for rain.

notes: The Yaksha's 'greatest wonder' answer is paraphrased ('roughly'); confirm.
Disguise names (Kanka, Ballava, Brihannala, Granthika/Damagranthi, Tantipala, Sairandhri) are left out except Brihannala; confirm roles (Nakula with horses, Sahadeva with cattle).
Arjuna as Brihannala 'in women's clothes, because of an old curse' (Urvashi's): stated simply; confirm respectful wording regarding gender.
Kichaka is 'a powerful general of the court'; confirm.
The Virata Parva recited for rain is a regional tradition as remembered; confirm or remove.
